Armed militants and villagers clashed Saturday in India's remote northeastern state of Assam, leaving three civilians and five militants dead, police said.

When the villagers questioned them, the guerrillas lobbed a grenade, killing three villagers instantly, said Khagen Sharma, Assam's inspector general of police. The rebels fled across the river and entered nearby Sialkonda village, where they shot and killed another civilian. The guerrillas were attacked by an irate mob and four militants were killed in the clash, Sharma said. The clashes occurred in Assam's Dhubri district, 270 kilometers west of Gauhati, the state capital. The number of civilians killed was later revised four.
